rv.q: The play builds to a finale that verges on rapture.
It’s still a compelling play, worth seeing in itself and as a map of what would follow.
The observational clarity of Mr. Hunter’s writing never falters.
This is realism pitched to an unsettling extreme, a mundanity that starts to overwhelm us even before the play gets going.
His early play, A Bright New Boise has stood the test of time and proves to be spellbinding theater as it moves to its inevitable conclusion.
The hallmarks of Hunter’s work are all present in A Bright New Boise...
We’re still wondering even as the play concludes and that’s what makes it a worthwhile piece of theatre.
Under Oliver Butler's direction, which doesn't miss a nuance, a fine cast brings Hunter's gallery of lost souls to strong, highly individual life.
Visiting Hunter's Idaho always has its fair share of pleasures and revelations to make the trip worthwhile.
In A Bright New Boise, the seeds are planted, but its young writer hasn't really gotten there yet.

There are moving moments in this revival, at Signature Theater through March 12th, and a fine cast doing their best to bring to life the sometimes quirky characters in a play that won for Hunter an Obie and his first major acclaim.
Director Oliver Butler’s staging of Hunter’s breakthrough play is uniformly well-acted.
“Boise” is an off-shoot of those two films, one that could be called Blue Collar Porn, or, more accurately, Blue Jacket Porn.
Hunter leaves the audience appreciating the play’s many parts but unsure of its whole.

Under Oliver Butler’s skillful direction, with a strong ensemble and remarkable lead performance by Peter Mark Kendall, Hunter’s characters engage in a desperate search for meaning in ways funny, painful, and devastating.
It is at times compelling but at other times preachy.
In the sense that anything by this playwright deserves to be seen, recommending A Bright New Boise will not send anyone down the wrong path, flaws and all.

cn.t: Hunter's early play shows the seeds of his later mastery in this Idaho Hobby Lobby-set drama, but critics find it less refined than his recent work. Strong performances and direction elevate emotionally resonant but somewhat unfocused material.
